candidates.attacker_control: Unauthenticated HTTP request header: Content-Type on any request to a Struts-mapped URL. The header must contain the literal substring `multipart/form-data` (so Dispatcher.wrapRequest picks the MultiPartRequestWrapper at Dispatcher.java:835) while remaining an invalid multipart media type for commons-fileupload, and must carry expression delimiters that OgnlTextParser evaluates. No application action, login, or interceptor configuration is needed: the evaluation occurs in PrepareOperations.wrapRequest (StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter.java:88-92) after createActionContext() has built the ValueStack.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked whether any control exists before the sink: (a) the bundle contains no InvalidContentTypeException message key, so the fallback default message really is used (struts-messages.properties:34-36, LocalizedTextUtil.java:665-676); (b) LocalizedTextUtil for class-based lookups does not sanitize/escape the default message (lines 660-683); (c) Dispatcher.wrapRequest's guard is a substring test, not a media-type parse (Dispatcher.java:834-838), and no other core filter validates Content-Type before wrapping (searched core dispatcher for getContentType()/multipart checks); (d) security hardening that does exist — SecurityMemberAccess excludedClasses/excludedPackageNamePatterns (struts-default.xml:41-55; SecurityMemberAccess.java:60-131), allowStaticMethodAccess=false (default.properties:208), DMI=false (default.properties:109), DefaultActionMapper allowedActionNames/action-prefix defaults (DefaultActionMapper.java:118-124) — mitigates naive payloads but was bypassable in this version via the context/`_memberAccess` route that this sink exposes; (e) the multipart wrapper is genuinely the default (struts-default.xml:82; default.properties:69).
candidates.impact: Expression/OGNL injection executed in the server's request-processing context before any action security checks. Historically this exact defect (S2-045) was exploited for remote code execution by manipulating the OGNL member-access sandbox via the value-stack context; at minimum it yields attacker-steered expression evaluation (information disclosure, error/DoS). The snapshot's sandbox lowering (struts.excludedClasses/excludedPackageNamePatterns, struts.ognl.allowStaticMethodAccess=false) does not remove the injection primitive, and this code baseline is the one associated with the known RCE. Exploitability of full RCE was not runtime-verified in this review.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) Application uses Struts core with the default multipart parser `struts.multipart.parser=jakarta` (core/src/main/resources/org/apache/struts2/default.properties:65-69; bean mapping in struts-default.xml:82) behind StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter/StrutsPrepareFilter or StrutsServlet (all call createActionContext before wrapRequest). 2) commons-fileupload 1.3.1 is pinned (pom.xml:681-684) and its InvalidContentTypeException message contains the raw content type; this library is outside the snapshot and was not executed. 3) The error key `struts.messages.upload.error.InvalidContentTypeException` is absent from struts-messages*.properties (only SizeLimitExceededException and IOException exist, core/src/main/resources/org/apache/struts2/struts-messages.properties:34-36), so the attacker-influenced default message is the one translated. 4) The `fileUpload` interceptor in defaultStack (struts-default.xml:193,291) propagates/uses the resulting error strings but is not required for the OGNL evaluation itself.
candidates.root_cause: JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage() passes the parser exception message as the `defaultMessage` argument to LocalizedTextUtil.findText (core/.../JakartaMultiPartRequest.java:118-124). When the error key is not present in any bundle, LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage() runs TextParseUtil.translateVariables(defaultMessage, valueStack) on that text (xwork-core/.../LocalizedTextUtil.java:660-683), which delegates to OgnlTextParser and evaluates every ${...}/%{...} fragment with stack.findValue (TextParseUtil.java:157-172; OgnlTextParser.java:10-82). The exception message in question comes from commons-fileupload's invalid-content-type failure and embeds the raw Content-Type request header (the RequestContext exposes req.getContentType() verbatim at JakartaMultiPartRequest.java:358-366), so attacker-controlled header text is OGNL-evaluated. Dispatcher.wrapRequest() only requires the header to *contain* the literal `multipart/form-data` to route the request into the multipart wrapper (Dispatcher.java:828-841); a header that contains that substring but is not a valid multipart media type makes commons-fileupload raise InvalidContentTypeException, whose message carries the whole header.
candidates.title: OGNL expression evaluation of attacker-controlled Content-Type via multipart error message (S2-045 pattern)
candidates.trace: StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter.doFilter -> PrepareOperations.createActionContext (ValueStack + context map installed; PrepareOperations.java:67-87) -> PrepareOperations.wrapRequest -> Dispatcher.wrapRequest checks content_type.contains("multipart/form-data") (Dispatcher.java:834-838) -> MultiPartRequestWrapper ctor -> JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse -> processUpload/parseRequest -> ServletFileUpload.parseRequest(createRequestContext(...)) with RequestContext.getContentType() = req.getContentType() (JakartaMultiPartRequest.java:185-189, 358-366) -> commons-fileupload throws an invalid-content-type exception whose message embeds the header -> parse() catch(Exception) -> buildErrorMessage(e, {}) (lines 101-108) -> LocalizedTextUtil.findText(JakartaMultiPartRequest.class, key, locale, e.getMessage(), args) (line 123) -> key not found in class/package/default bundles -> LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage falls back to defaultMessage (lines 665-671) and calls TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack) (line 675) -> TextParseUtil.translateVariables(openChars {'$','%'}) -> OgnlTextParser.evaluate -> ParsedValueEvaluator -> stack.findValue(parsedValue, asType) (TextParseUtil.java:159-167) => OGNL evaluation of the attacker-controlled header content inside the request ValueStack context. The same unneutralized pattern exists in MultiPartRequestWrapper.buildErrorMessage (lines 99-105) and JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage/buildMessage (lines 527-546), i.e. one root cause with several call sites, not separate findings.
candidates.unverified: 1) commons-fileupload 1.3.1 is a binary dependency, not in the snapshot; its exact InvalidContentTypeException message text (embedding the raw Content-Type) is taken from documented library behavior and was not executed. 2) The OGNL sandbox bypass required for full RCE was not run or proven; the historical exploitability of this code baseline is background knowledge, not runtime evidence. 3) No build/tests/scanners were run (none are present in the snapshot; relation index is navigation-only). 4) Whether a particular deployed application configures a non-default multipart parser or a front proxy that normalizes Content-Type was not assessed.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-917 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement (OGNL expression injection); potential CWE-94 code injection

coverage_summary: Source scope: 2,866 files under the assigned root (core, xwork-core, 28 plugins, archetypes, apps, assembly), all model-visible; get_source_scope reports 0 exclusions by size/sensitive-name/symlink and a policy that skips binary-like files (no NUL-detected files were material to this review). P1 relation index reports complete coverage: 2,866/2,866 files indexed, 0 files missing from the index, 0 source-hash mismatches, 18,280 symbols / 37,151 call records / 461 facts; the index was used only for navigation and every cited edge was verified in source text. Primary files read and traced end-to-end: core dispatcher/multipart (JakartaMultiPartRequest, JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest, MultiPartRequestWrapper), Dispatcher.wrapRequest, StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter/PrepareOperations/StrutsServlet, FilterDispatcher, DefaultStaticContentLoader, DefaultActionMapper, ServletActionRedirectResult, FileUploadInterceptor, core default.properties/struts-default.xml/struts-messages*.properties, xwork-core LocalizedTextUtil/TextParseUtil/OgnlTextParser/OgnlValueStack/OgnlUtil/SecurityMemberAccess/ParametersInterceptor/CookieInterceptor, plugins rest (XStreamHandler, ContentType handlers), struts1, and pom.xml dependency versions. Note: the snapshot contains no test sources at all, and no code was executed.
limitations: No build, test, scanner, or exploit execution was performed (none is available in this run); the finding is a source-level lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.

The commons-fileupload 1.3.1 jar is a binary dependency and is not part of the snapshot; its exception text (which embeds the raw Content-Type) was not read or executed, so that link is based on documented library behavior.

Full RCE impact depends on the OGNL member-access sandbox bypass; the excludedClasses/excludedPackageNamePatterns and allowStaticMethodAccess=false hardening in this snapshot were inspected but the bypass was not reproduced.
The P1 relation index is syntactic/navigation-only and explicitly does not prove reachability, data flow, or exploitability; no SAST or ground-truth findings were loaded.

Coverage of the wider product surface (tag libraries/JSP views, portlet/json/jasperreports/tiles/dwr plugins, demo apps, archetypes) was sampled rather than exhaustively audited; the one-candidate cap also means alternative leads were not developed to the same depth.

rejected_leads.lead: REST plugin deserialization: XStreamHandler.toObject() parses the request body with a plain `new XStream()` and xstream.fromXML(reader, target), with no type whitelist (plugins/rest/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/rest/handler/XStreamHandler.java:43-50; handler registered for application/xml in plugins/rest/src/main/resources/struts-plugin.xml:35).
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible S2-052-style unsafe deserialization, but it requires the optional REST plugin enabled in the application and XML content negotiation, and exploitability rests entirely on external XStream default behavior not visible in the snapshot. Kept as an unconfirmed alternative to the core, default-configuration multipart OGNL path.

rejected_leads.lead: Struts 1 plugin message handling: Struts1Action.addActionMessage(getText(msg.getKey(), ...)) passes an ActionMessage key into getText, whose default-message fallback is OGNL-translated (plugins/struts1/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/s1/Struts1Action.java:101-109; Struts1Factory.java:129-145).
rejected_leads.reason: Same underlying 'untrusted text reaches LocalizedTextUtil default-message OGNL evaluation' mechanism and matches the known S2-048 pattern, but attacker control requires application code to place user input into an ActionMessage key plus the optional struts1 plugin; the in-repo sink alone does not demonstrate an attacker-controlled flow.

rejected_leads.lead: Namespace/redirect OGNL evaluation: ServletActionRedirectResult.execute applies conditionalParse to actionName/namespace/method (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/ServletActionRedirectResult.java:165-180) and DefaultActionMapper exposes alwaysSelectFullNamespace (DefaultActionMapper.java:197-200).
rejected_leads.reason: S2-057-style path requires the non-default `struts.mapper.alwaysSelectFullNamespace=true` setting and a redirect/chain result configuration that consumes a URL-derived namespace; the null-namespace branch uses the proxy namespace without conditionalParse, so no complete attacker-controlled flow to OGNL evaluation was verified in this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: Action-prefix/DMI URL manipulation in DefaultActionMapper (`action:`, `method:` prefixes, `!method` syntax).
rejected_leads.reason: Appears hardened in this baseline: allowActionPrefix defaults to false, action names are constrained by the allowedActionNames pattern, and struts.enable.DynamicMethodInvocation defaults to false (DefaultActionMapper.java:115-124,187-215; default.properties:109), so the historical S2-016/S2-032-style routes were not supported by the reviewed code.

summary: Defensive source review of the Apache Struts 2.3.20.1-SNAPSHOT tree (2,866 files: core, xwork-core, 28 plugins, sample apps). The single strongest plausible issue is an OGNL/expression-injection path in the core multipart handling: the Jakarta multipart parser feeds an attacker-influenced exception message (which embeds the raw Content-Type header) into LocalizedTextUtil.findText as the default message, and that text is then evaluated as OGNL (${...}/%{...}) against the request ValueStack during PrepareOperations.wrapRequest — the historical S2-045 pattern. The default parser is `jakarta`, the path is reached before any action/interceptor executes, and the repo contains no content-type validation or bundle key that would neutralize the attacker text, so this is a pre-action request-processing injection primitive (RCE potential given the OGNL sandbox weaknesses of this version). No runtime confirmation was performed.
